                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being attacked with a knife. Physical examination shows a 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm. An MRI of the right arm shows damage to a nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Loss of sensation over which of the following areas is most likely in this patient?

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this case, the 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm and the MRI findings suggest damage to a nerve located between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. The ulnar nerve runs in this region and is responsible for sensory innervation to the palmar surface of the little finger. Therefore, the most likely area of sensation loss in this patient is the palmar surface of the little finger. The reasoning aligns with the consensus that the ulnar nerve is primarily responsible for this sensory distribution, confirming the option regarding loss of sensation in the little finger.
